title: Reviewer subagent output
description: Shape returned by a reviewer subagent inside an agent-skill review (angular-review and variants). See each skill's ORCHESTRATION.md Step 3 for the prompt that produces this.

$schema.description: URI of this schema (optional, useful for editor autocomplete).

agent.description: Identifier of the reviewer subagent that produced this output (e.g. angular-security-reviewer).

findings.description: List of findings. Empty array means the reviewer found no issues in its scope.

ruleId.description: Rule identifier, prefix+number (e.g. R-SEC-003, R-KATA-001, R-RUNTIME-12).

severity.description: Closed set. The orchestrator's aggregation step relies on these exact values for verdict computation.

domain.description: Free-form domain tag (e.g. security, architecture, performance, a11y, project).

file.description: Repo-relative path to the offending file.

snippet.description: Short excerpt of the offending line (one line, no surrounding context).

message.description: What is wrong, in human-readable prose.

suggestion.description: How to fix it, in human-readable prose.

source.description: Pointer to the canonical reference (angular.dev URL, internal RFC, kata brief, etc.).

evidence.description: Optional structured proof backing the finding. Required by skills enforcing evidence-based review (e.g. the kata variant for Step 6 DOM findings). When present, MUST include at least 'kind'.

kind.description: How the finding was obtained. 'dom' = measured via Playwright/MCP at runtime; 'test' = from a versioned test run; 'static' = from diff/source inspection; 'manual' = author-asserted; 'not_checked' = constraint not validated this run.

expected.description: Expected value or behaviour (e.g. 'top = 25% of container height for 12:00').

selector.description: DOM selector used to locate the element (CSS selector, ARIA query, data-testid).

measurement.description: How the value was measured (e.g. 'getBoundingClientRect().top relative to .calendar container, viewport 1280×720').

confidence.description: Reviewer confidence in the measurement. 'high' = direct DOM read with stable selector; 'medium' = heuristic selector; 'low' = inferred or fallback.
